beats.lead: The famous story says the accident made him a different man
beats.text: The record is thinner than that.
beats.note: Malcolm Macmillan, who studied the case closely, says a personality change did occur but did not last much longer than two to three years.

beats.name: Phineas Gage
beats.role: Railroad foreman. On 13 September, near Cavendish, Vermont, a tamping iron went through his head. He was conscious and speaking within minutes.

beats.note: It entered below his left cheekbone, left through the top of his skull, and landed roughly 25 metres behind him.

beats.name: Stagecoach driver, Chile
beats.role: Gage drove six-horse coaches on the Valparaiso to Santiago route. Macmillan reads his hiring as evidence that the worst changes were temporary.

beats.note: That was eight years after he died. Little was recorded about his personality before or after the accident.

beats.text: The iron went through his head. The legend went further than the evidence.

beats.line: Check the case notes before the legend.
